feedback: Accepted. Exact paper format is respected (REWARD_MACHINE/STATES/INITIAL_STATE/FINAL_STATES/TRANSITION_FUNCTION/REWARD_FUNCTION), FINAL_STATES is nonempty, u6 is declared in STATES and is accepting: it is reachable (e.g., u0 ->(pickup) u1 ->(at_exit & holding_box) u6) and is the success sink. Semantic fidelity is good: the terminal 1.0 fires only on at_exit & holding_box, and the distinctive 'pick it up again on the very next move' clause is correctly enforced — a fall (u1 -> u2 or u3 -> u5) must be followed by holding_box on the very next step (-> u3, +0.2 for the first fall) or the run dead-ends in absorbing u4 and forfeits the terminal reward, which matches the literal timing requirement; missing the recovery but still exiting with the box correctly pays 0. Irrelevant events (siren_ringing, switch_toggled, drops, done, turns) are absorbed by per-state else self-loops in all seven states; per-state guards are mutually exclusive and exhaustive with else last. Only domain predicates are used, with box_fell correctly treated as a one-step event and holding_box/at_exit as conditions; at_exit appears only on terminal edges, consistent with it holding on the last step only and the no-fall/no-toggle-on-exit-step constraints. All seven states are reachable and u6 is reachable from every live state. Rewards are nonnegative, bounded (max 1.0), and never placed on self-loops. Non-blocking issues to clean up: (1) dead transitions: (u0, box_fell)->u2 and (u0, at_exit & holding_box)->u6 (the pickup step already leaves u0, and the first fall comes 2-6 steps after it; the exit step cannot coincide with a pickup), (u2, box_fell)->u5 and (u5, box_fell)->u5 (any further fall requires an intervening pickup, which leaves u2/u5; there are at most two falls), (u5, at_exit & holding_box)->u6, and the else self-loops of u2/u5 (guards 1-4 already cover every proposition combination there); (2) the 0.2 reward sits on the dead edge (u2, box_fell, u5) while the live second-fall edges (u3, box_fell, u5) and (u5, holding_box & !at_exit, u3) carry no reward, so the second fall's recovery is enforced but unshaped and the shaping is asymmetric — either move the 0.2 onto those edges or merge u5 into u2 for symmetry and compactness; (3) note that the strict next-step pickup is physically impossible in episodes where the front cell is blocked at the fall (box lands right/behind/left), making u6 unreachable there even for optimal play; this follows from the task's literal wording rather than an RM defect, but it is worth documenting.

All five environment-declared propositions are implemented exactly, with no extras and none missing. `siren_ringing` returns `env.siren_ringing` directly (persistent condition, matches truth table). `switch_toggled` checks membership of "toggle" in `env.events_this_step` (event, matches documented source). `holding_box` checks `env.carrying is not None and env.carrying.type == "box"` (persistent condition, matches). `box_fell` checks "fall" in `env.events_this_step` (event, matches). `at_exit` reads the grid cell at `env.agent_pos` with a proper `is not None` guard before reading `.type == "goal"` (persistent condition, matches the documented expression; explicit indexing is equivalent to unpacking). No imports, no actions, no side effects, no mutation of the environment or episode memory, no reliance on `previous_valuation` beyond the documented API (not needed here since the environment exposes `events_this_step` for events and direct state for conditions). Syntax is valid Python and all expressions are safe under the documented API: grid access is guarded, `carrying` is None-guarded, `agent_pos` indexing is in bounds. Boolean fidelity holds for all five predicates.
